Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Singapore on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investment (1985, as amended)

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland concerning the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1986)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on 13 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Management (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, adopted 2024, effective 1 November 2024); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations of the People's Bank of China applicable to specific non-financial institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified true copy) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies in the jurisdiction of origin of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive authentication path: (a) if the issuing state is a Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, the certificate is notarized by a local notary and then certified by an Apostille issued by the designated competent authority of that state; (b) if the issuing state is not an Apostille Party, the certificate is notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent, and then legalized by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that state. The two paths are parallel, independent, and may never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active State of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Current Companies Registry or State Corporate Registrar of the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local licensed notary, followed exclusively by either an Apostille (if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member) or consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate (if not a member). No document shall carry both Apostille and consular legalization consecutively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the formation of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture and granting Power of Attorney to the designated incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign investor, acting under its constitutional documents and statutory minute book
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be notarized at the place of execution; the notarized instrument is then submitted to the competent authority for Apostille in an Apostille Convention state, or to the Chinese Consulate for legalization in a non-member state. Each path applies separately depending on state membership and no sequential mixing is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or official Companies Registry of the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The registry-issued or notarized certified copy, after notarization if necessary, is authenticated either by Apostille (Apostille Convention state) or by China consular legalization (non-member state). The two methods are exclusive and cannot be cumulatively applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter on financial standing of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank where the foreign investor maintains its principal corporate account, issued on bank letterhead and signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature and bank seal must be notarized; the notarized letter then undergoes either Apostille certification (in Apostille member jurisdictions) or Chinese consular legalization (in non-member jurisdictions), depending solely on the country of the issuing bank. No chain combining both paths is allowed.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, and the PBOC/Public Security domestic blacklists for money laundering and terrorism. All direct and ultimate beneficial owners, directors, senior officers, material counterparties, and intended payment-rail beneficiaries (Stripe and Wise) must be screened for politically exposed persons (PEP) status, including family members and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, at every ownership change, and continuously through automated daily list updates for five years, with fully auditable screening reports. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, tax-haven residence, or adverse media; simplified due diligence may be applied for the low-risk standard tier only after confirming no hit in any screening list and completion of government beneficial ownership filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration Management System (operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation and its provincial/municipal bureaux, with an online English-facing service named National Enterprise Name Reservation Service Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese name of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture must adopt the four-tier statutory naming structure: administrative region, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and corporate form suffix (Limited Company). An English name may be registered as an additional name and must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the approved Chinese name, with Hanyu Pinyin romanization used for scrutiny. Simplified Chinese characters are mandatory; traditional Chinese, Japanese Kanji or Korean Hanja are not accepted. The distinctive name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing name in the national registry, and foreign investors must submit an explanation of meaning and transliteration for examination.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects the name application, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the supervisory authority one level above the rejecting local SAMR within 15 working days from receipt of the written refusal, specifying legal grounds and attaching the original refusal notice. If the reconsideration is unfavorable, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months from the reconsideration decision. In parallel, the applicant may submit a new name application using a revised distinctive name to preserve the incorporation timeline. Where the rejection is based on confusing similarity, the applicant may request a comparative report from SAMR and may substantiate goodwill, prior registration certificates, or a written consent from the prior name holder. An approved name reservation may be extended once for an additional 180 days upon showing justification before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Sino-foreign equity joint venture providing outsourced fractional CFO advisory and multicurrency ledger bookkeeping under ISIC 6920, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by SAMR, local tax authorities, and commercial banks unless the registered address is a physical suite where the legal representative, corporate seal, accounting books, invoices, and staff are actually present. Banks such as those used by Stripe and Wise require physical visitor verification and address inspection. In special economic zones including the Shanghai Free Trade Zone, address hosting may be accepted for a transitional period, but tax and AML regulators require a real lease, lease registration with the local housing/tax bureau, and evidence of management presence. A virtual office with only a mail-forwarding service carries an estimated 40-60% rejection risk for bank account opening and could trigger SAMR de-registration of the address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspection checklist: 1) actual address matches registered address; 2) original lease contract and rental payment records; 3) payroll and social insurance records of staff physically present; 4) original ledgers, invoices, accounting vouchers and financial statements; 5) presence of the legal representative or designated senior manager; 6) IT systems and secure server storage for client financial data. Quantified risk: random SAMR/tax inspections for low-risk standard-tier enterprises occur at 2-5% annually; if an annual report flags discrepancies or a complaint is lodged, the likelihood rises to 75%. Estimated probability of an unannounced visit during the first 12 months of operation is 25%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise establishment registration fee for the Sino-foreign equity joint venture (including business license and company seal filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: no official registration fee is charged by SAMR for foreign-invested enterprises as of 2024; this item is zero per national fee waiver notices.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise name pre-reservation and name clearance filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SAMR local bureau via the National Enterprise Name Registration Management System
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: free of charge on the online portal.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of foreign investor board resolution and power of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed notary public in the foreign investor's jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark USD 50-200 per notarial instrument.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille certification of the documentary bundle (5 documents, Apostille Convention member state path)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated Competent Authority for Apostilles of the foreign jurisdiction (e.g., Secretary of State or Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark USD 30-80 per document; estimated 5 documents at USD 50 each.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of the documentary bundle (alternative path, only if foreign jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in the issuing state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff USD 40-100 per document plus consular service charges; alternative to the Apostille line and mutually exclusive with it.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of the 5-document legal bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation company or notary translation office authorized in China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark USD 20-60 per page; estimated 10 pages at USD 30 per page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner information collection and submission to PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PRC filing agent or external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government fee; professional administrative filing fee benchmark USD 100-300.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal retainer for JV incorporation, name clearance, UBO piercing, and pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged outside law firm licensed by the PRC Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Sino-foreign equity joint venture incorporation in China ranges from USD 4,000 to USD 8,000, depending on complexity; fixed retainer quoted.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Deposit for physical registered office lease (3 months) to evidence commercial substance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord / real estate lessor under a registered lease in China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark 2-6 months of rent for a small office suite; estimated monthly rent USD 1,000 for a single professional workstation and records room.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 2, 4, 7, 47-55 and 68-74; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 15, 16 and 22; Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law (State Council Decree No. 723), Articles 5 and 10. The former Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Law is repealed; Sino-foreign JVs are now subject to national treatment and unified market registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Market Supervision Administration (MSA) under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), local district-level registration bureau at the jurisdiction of the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the authenticated Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture under current law. The amount, currency and payment schedule are fixed in the Articles of Association. No blocked escrow account or paid-in capital proof is required for incorporation; however, Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law requires shareholders to fully pay subscribed capital within five years of establishment, and any reduction or restructuring of capital requires a special shareholders' resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN_JV_LTD] (the 'Company'), adopted in writing by all directors and ratified by the shareholders, in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The Board, having verified the certificate of incorporation and the Unified Social Credit Code, resolves that: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The board ratifies the registered capital of RMB [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares. Each shareholder's subscription schedule as set out in the Articles of Association is confirmed, and each shareholder is obliged to pay the subscribed capital in full within the statutory period, in no event later than five years after the date of establishment, without any requirement that capital be held in a blocked escrow account except to the extent mandated by applicable foreign exchange control or industry rules. 2. Banking Authorization. The Chairman, the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open and maintain bank accounts in licensed banks in China, to designate account mandates, and to execute banking documentation. The bank mandate shall require two authorized signatories for any payment exceeding the equivalent of RMB 500,000, and all internet-banking users must be approved by the Board. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Association and certified by the business license. The officers are directed to execute the lease, register the office with the Market Supervision Administration, and display the business license and any required permits at the principal place of business. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Name] is appointed Legal Representative and Chairman; [Name] is appointed General Manager; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] is appointed Supervisor. Each officer shall hold office for the term specified in the Articles of Association and shall exercise no greater powers than those conferred by law. The Legal Representative is specially authorized to sign tax filings, employment registration, bank account forms and administrative permit applications, and to appear before the taxation authority, the local Market Supervision Administration, the local finance bureau and the social insurance authority in connection with the Company's formation. 5. Seals, Books and Corporate Records. The Board adopts the company seal, the financial seal, the contract seal and the legal representative seal, and establishes accounting books and statutory records in compliance with the Accounting Law. These resolutions are effective immediately upon adoption and may be implemented by the officers without further shareholder approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Market Entity Pre-Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) national online registration portal / local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to the SAMR online registration portal using real-name authentication of the intended Legal Representative and foreign shareholder representative. Submit a name reservation application indicating the company type as limited liability company and the line of business as accounting, bookkeeping, financial advisory and virtual CFO services. The proposed name must contain a distinctive trade name, a section identifying the industry, and the company type suffix. The application must also select the foreign-invested company type under the Foreign Investment Law and indicate the jurisdiction of the registered office. The system will issue a Name Reservation Notice valid for 60 days, during which the incorporation application must be filed.
required_dossiers: Legal Representative and Supervisor identity certificates
Foreign shareholder passport or entity certificate with notarization and legalization
Power of attorney for the formation agent if any
Proposed name list of at least three alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected as identical, misleading or contrary to name regulations, review the rejection ground and immediately submit corrected alternative names through the same portal. The rejected name is released after the statutory objection hold and may be reserved again only after the system grants a new approval notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Authentication of Formation Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration registration guidance desk, Chinese consular authorities and approved notary authorities for foreign investor documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the fully executed Articles of Association, the shareholders' capital contribution agreement, the list of directors, the list of supervisors and the proposed Legal Representative appointment. Foreign shareholders' certificates of incorporation, passports and good-standing evidence must be notarized in the country of issue and legalized by the Chinese consulate or, where the Hague Apostille Convention applies, apostilled. The registered office lease must be accompanied by the property ownership certificate or the landlord's written consent. All non-Chinese documents must be translated into Chinese by a certified translation agency for MSA acceptance.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Capital contribution schedule
Registered office lease and property certificate or landlord consent
Notarized and legalized foreign shareholder identity and good-standing certificates
Appointment forms for Legal Representative, board members, Supervisor and Chief Financial Officer
Power of attorney for formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or legalization is deemed insufficient, obtain a supplementary notarial certificate in the foreign jurisdiction and re-authenticate the document. If the registered office proof fails, substitute a compliant rent-free use letter or a new lease and resubmit the corrected dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Submission and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration center or SAMR one-stop online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Establishment Registration, the authenticated Articles of Association, the identity and qualification certificates, the registered office documents and the constitutional list of officers to the MSA. Execute the declaration that all information is true and complete, and verify that all fields are populated for the Foreign Investment Information Report in the integrated market registration system. The MSA will review the application, issue the business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code, and return the approved formation record. The company is legally established on the date of license issuance, and the first board resolution may then be adopted.
required_dossiers: Approved Name Reservation Notice
Application for Establishment Registration form
Notarized Articles of Association
Registered office legal-use proof
Identity certificates of all directors and officers
Capital contribution schedule
Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a correction notice, remedy the cited defect within 10 working days by amending the Articles or supplementary documents. If the application lapses, resubmit without loss of priority and without an additional administrative fee, preserving the earliest filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registration and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local State Taxation Administration office, social insurance registration window, labor administration and a licensed commercial bank authorized to handle foreign exchange
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is obtained, apply to the tax authority for tax registration and confirmation of the fiscal identification number under the Unified Social Credit Code. Complete social insurance and employment registration, and file the labor contract records. Open a basic RMB deposit account at a licensed bank and, where foreign investors will remit capital, open a foreign exchange capital account. Confirm the bank mandate using the First Board Resolution and the Legal Representative identification. These steps are prerequisites for invoice issuance and for making social insurance and tax payments.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Articles of Association and license
Legal Representative ID and board resolution on bank mandate
First Board Resolution
Office occupancy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration fails because the business scope is inconsistent, apply for amendment of the business scope to include bookkeeping agency services before completing the tax registration. If the bank rejects the mandate, issue a corrective board resolution and resubmit all authorized signatory identity documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Service-Sector Bookkeeping Agency Authorization (Professional Statutory License)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Finance Bureau accounting and bookkeeping agency approval section / provincial finance department online administrative approval window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company will provide outsourced CFO, bookkeeping and accounting services to third-party clients, it must obtain the Bookkeeping Agency Permit before executing paid bookkeeping contracts in mainland China. Submit the permit application through the finance bureau's online administrative service portal, describing professional staffing, internal control policies, data privacy safeguards for client ledgers and the registered office as the place of performance. The finance bureau will verify that the company employs the required qualified accounting personnel and will inspect the internal control manual. After issuance, display the permit at the registered office and register the agency with the taxation authority for bookkeeping agent reporting.
required_dossiers: Application form for Bookkeeping Agency Permit
Business License and Unified Social Credit Code
Certificates and employment contracts of qualified accounting professionals
Internal control and confidentiality manual
Registered office lease and workplace compliance certificate
Criminal record and professional discipline certificate for the responsible principal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the finance bureau queries professional qualifications, supplement the file with the accountant's continuing education records or replace the responsible principal. If the application is rejected, file an administrative reconsideration with the provincial finance department within 60 days of receipt of the rejection notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable—no industrial, manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing site is involved under ISIC 6920. The relevant statutory service-sector authority for the required operating authorization is the Local Municipal Finance Bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bookkeeping Agency Permit (service-sector statutory operating permit under the Interim Measures for Agency Bookkeeping Administration); no industrial operating permit applies to the virtual CFO and outsourced accounting activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable—no construction, manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing project triggers environmental permitting in the Ministry of Ecology and Environment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable—exempt from Full EIA Report and from Environmental Registration for this pure digital/consulting service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable—no process wastewater, volatile organic compounds or hazardous waste streams. Only ordinary municipal solid waste sorting and e-waste disposal rules apply to the office operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable—no industrial fire permit or civil-defense clearance is required for virtual CFO services. The leased office must nevertheless comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, including maintained portable extinguishers, unobstructed exits, emergency lighting, and lawful occupation approval under the applicable fire and workplace-safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online filing is administered through the nationwide E-Tax Administration (electronic tax bureau) portal and the E-Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain a business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation; the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code is automatically created and serves as the statutory Tax Identification Number for tax filing and VAT purposes. Step 2: Within 30 days after business license issuance, complete taxpayer registration in the local STA E-Tax Administration portal, submitting entity details, registered address, accounting standards, legal representative, and bank settlement account information. Step 3: Confirm VAT taxpayer classification: small-scale taxpayer or general VAT taxpayer. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; otherwise the entity may elect small-scale status subject to statutory limits. Step 4: Activate e-invoice entitlement and obtain the tax control number through the STA E-Invoice Service Platform. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese establishment, the Chinese payer or withholding agent must first complete withholding tax registration in the E-Tax portal. If the non-resident entity itself needs to issue Chinese VAT invoices or conducts continuous taxable activities in China, it must obtain a temporary tax registration and a dedicated taxpayer identification number from the local STA office where the activities occur.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime and does not grant hybrid mismatch elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) election between small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment and general VAT taxpayer treatment; (ii) election of the simplified levy-rate method for certain VAT-taxable services; and (iii) non-resident election to apply China-foreign income tax treaty protections through the non-resident tax filing procedure. No pass-through entity election is available for a Sino-foreign equity joint venture.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, administered by the State Taxation Administration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; monthly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 (quarterly RMB 300,000) qualify for small-scale taxpayer VAT exemption. All enterprises are required to obtain VAT registration after business license issuance; there is no turnover exemption for entity registration itself.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates fully digitalized electronic invoices through the STA E-Invoice Service Platform. VAT special invoices and ordinary invoices must carry a unique digital tax-control number and be transmitted in real time to the STA through the Golden Tax Phase IV system. General VAT taxpayers using API integration must generate invoices only after online clearance and digital stamping; issuance of invalid, unauthorized, or manually pre-printed special invoices is prohibited. Any anomaly in invoice quota, sequencing, or declared versus invoiced amounts triggers automatic risk alerts, suspension of invoice quotas, and on-site tax inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exports, zero-rating applies when goods are physically exported from mainland China and supported by an official customs export declaration. For cross-border services, zero-rating or VAT exemption applies when the services are supplied to an overseas enterprise or individual, are wholly consumed outside mainland China, and fall within the published catalogue of cross-border taxable services. For virtual CFO, bookkeeping, and management consulting services, the substantive criteria are: an overseas service recipient, no direct linkage to Chinese land or goods, a legally valid cross-border service agreement, and foreign-currency consideration received through an authorized bank. If these conditions are not met, the supply is treated as domestic and subject to VAT at 6%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export commercial invoice and packing list
Cross-border service contract or purchase order with the overseas counterparty
Proof of overseas recipient registration or tax residency
Customs export cargo inspection report where physical goods are involved
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and General Administration of Customs jointly verify export declarations, foreign-currency receipts, and invoice history. If zero-rating is claimed without verifiable export, if the foreign-currency proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, or if documentation is discovered to be falsified, the tax authority will claw back the VAT rebate or zero-rated refund, impose daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% on the unpaid tax, and charge an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulent export tax refund cases may be referred for criminal prosecution under Chinese law, resulting in confiscation, fines, and imprisonment for responsible officers. Unfiled or incorrectly documented export claims also trigger customs penalties and revocation of export rebate qualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign exchange administration authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility consistent with IMF Article VIII, but the capital account remains subject to comprehensive approval, registration, and reporting controls. A Sino-foreign equity joint venture may accept FDI capital only after the investor and the venture complete SAFE registration, open a foreign exchange capital account at a SAFE-designated bank, and submit a genuine-use undertaking. Foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to China and either retained in foreign exchange accounts or converted to RMB only through banks applying the Foreign Investment Negative List and capital-expenditure rules. Profit remittance is not prohibited, but before dividends can be paid abroad the JV must complete annual statutory audit, settle all corporate income tax and withholding tax liabilities, secure board approval, and demonstrate that paid-in registered capital is in place and not damaged by losses. Current-account payments for professional services are normally allowed without SAFE pre-approval if the underlying contracts, invoices, tax records, and business purpose are genuine and consistent. This creates an operating environment where licensed domestic banks remain mandatory and offshore digital EMIs cannot serve as primary treasury rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods exports, 100% of declared export proceeds must be repatriated to China within 180 days from the date of customs declaration or the approved deferred-collection maturity. There is no fixed surrender ratio or forced conversion benchmark: an exporter may keep the repatriated foreign currency in an SAFE-approved foreign exchange settlement account or sell it voluntarily to the bank. The receiving bank must match the wire to the customs export declaration through SAFE's monitoring systems and record the receipt under the exporter's trade item; any mismatch, delayed collection, or offshore retention must be explained and, where applicable, approved by SAFE. Service export receipts follow the same 100% repatriation principle through the service trade and balance-of-payments reporting mechanism.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account, RMB Basic Deposit Account, and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall viability is Low for primary account opening and Low-to-Medium for auxiliary payment orchestration. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise and Stripe are not licensed by SAFE or the PBOC as depository institutions in mainland China, cannot open domestic RMB or FX accounts for a China-incorporated JV, cannot process FDI capital injection, cannot submit SAFE declarations, and cannot issue bank capital-verification certificates. They can, at best, operate as a front-end invoicing or payment collection tool where the actual settlement is executed by a Chinese licensed bank, or as a non-resident treasury overlay only after funds have legally left China and are held in a separately licensed offshore account. The JV must maintain its statutory Chinese bank account as the sole account of record for tax, FX, and capital-control purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory legal representatives and authorized financial officers must generally appear physically at the Chinese bank branch for initial account opening; remote-only or consular proxy opening is not a standard option for a Sino-foreign equity JV. PBOC account-opening rules require original company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, the legal representative's identity certificate, and physical execution of account documents. Some banks permit a remote video interview after the in-branch appearance of the local finance manager or a notarially appointed authorized signatory, but the legal representative's identity verification cannot be fully bypassed for the primary operational account. Foreign parent shareholders must provide notarized and legalized corporate resolutions, board minutes, and identity documents; if the legal representative is outside China, a China-resident authorized person with an express notarized power of attorney is usually required to attend in person and be registered as the account handler.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership chain includes an offshore parent or trust jurisdiction with opacity concerns, nominee directors, or a PEP-connected investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submitted file must contain notarized certificates of incorporation and registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain; a signed group structure chart naming all direct and indirect shareholders; full passport or national identity copies of every individual holding 5% or more; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; professional background CVs; and, where PEP or sanctions-list media hits exist, an enhanced due diligence package with bank reference letters, audited financial statements, and legal opinions from counsel in the relevant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection arrives from a parent treasury that is not the registered shareholder of record, or the remittance references a purpose other than capital contribution to avoid tax or FX monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The JV must show the SAFE FDI registration notice; the investment agreement and articles of association; a board resolution confirming the shareholder of record and the exact capital injection amount; a full source-of-funds file covering the remitting entity's bank statements and audited accounts for at least 12 months; confirmation that the remitting entity is either the registered shareholder or a fully disclosed treasury subsidiary with an internal funding mandate; and a written reconciliation between the bank wire and the CPA capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue model depends on recurring small cross-border payments through online platforms such as Stripe or Wise, creating an appearance of unauthorized money service business or third-party payment aggregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the China business license and VAT and corporate income tax registration showing the lawful scope of fractional CFO advisory and bookkeeping; execute master service agreements with named resident and non-resident clients; issue VAT-compliant invoices in the JV's name; produce a payment-flow diagram showing Stripe and Wise only as licensed acquiring or financial-technology networks, with settlement ultimately to a Chinese bank; retain detailed timesheets, deliverables, and engagement letters; and include a board-approved compliance policy prohibiting collection of third-party funds and invoice multiplication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend or profit remittance to the foreign shareholder before statutory audit, tax clearance, and capital-account verification have been completed; losses in the JV balance sheet or registered capital impairment are hidden.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the statutory audit report issued by a PRC licensed CPA firm; corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax payment vouchers; tax registration and filing confirmation; board or shareholders resolution declaring distributable profits; a balance sheet and profit appropriation statement demonstrating positive retained earnings and full paid-in registered capital; and the SAFE foreign exchange profit-remittance form signed by the authorized bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital is: (i) complete post-incorporation FDI registration with SAFE or its delegated bank and confirm the JV business is outside the Foreign Investment Negative List; (ii) open a foreign exchange capital account at a SAFE-qualified domestic bank; (iii) instruct the foreign parent to wire the contribution via SWIFT MT103 with remittance purpose Investment Capital Contribution (FDI) and the registered parent company name; (iv) the Chinese receiving bank verifies the beneficiary, remitter, and registered name, records the payment in the SAFE monitoring system, and credits the FX capital account; (v) convert only for approved operating expenditures using the RMB capital settlement account, requiring a declaration that funds will not be used for prohibited portfolio investment, entrusted lending, or real estate outside the permitted scope; (vi) after the contribution is fully paid, appoint a PRC registered accountant to issue the capital verification report and update SAFE registration. Remittances should not be fragmented to avoid reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a virtual CFO consultancy, outbound payments are mostly current-account service fees, royalties, and professional fees payable under master service agreements. The cleanest rail is SWIFT MT103 for each service disbursement, supported by the agreed contract, invoice, service delivery records, applicable tax withholding certificate, and bank truthfulness review. The JV may buy FX at the onshore bank's real-time rate and remit subject to current-account documentation. For merchandise trade embedded in a broader group, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections remain available for goods, but the ISIC 6920 entity should not use inventory-based trade finance unless actual goods are transacted; using L/C or documentary collections without underlying goods movement will create AML and export-control red flags. Direct offshore settlement via Stripe or Wise is not a permissible outbound rail for corporate ledger or fee payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with a SAFE-licensed bank, typically up to 12 months or aligned to the underlying trade or financing exposure
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps for long-term FDI exposure, limited to the registered capital and loan maturity profile
FX swaps for temporary working capital and conversion liquidity, subject to underlying commercial flow and bank credit line

Offshore NDFs are not a permissible onshore treasury instrument for the JV; access may be considered only through a licensed non-resident parent treasury centre outside China after funds have been legally remitted offshore

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (annual market entity annual return) to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Regulation Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the immediately preceding financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish by 30 June results in inclusion on the List of Enterprises Operating Abnormally; continued failure for three years triggers the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, administrative restrictions on registration/credit/licensing, and ultimate compulsory deregistration/administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (foreign-invested enterprise annual reporting under the Foreign Investment Law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) jointly with SAMR through the Foreign Investment Information Reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late/inaccurate filing invokes a MOFCOM correction order and administrative penalties; unresolved non-compliance is recorded in national credit files, may cancel preferential foreign investment treatment, and supports loss of good standing/compulsory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Final Settlement (annual CIT return and settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / local competent tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on overdue tax; underpayment sanctions of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount; enforced collection via asset seizure, bank account freeze, and legal representative travel/exit restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Independent CPA Audit Report (mandatory audit for Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: PRC-registered CPA firm; audit report attached to SAMR/MOFCOM annual filings and retained for local tax and SAFE foreign exchange inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the relevant annual filings are submitted; practical deadline 30 June, or 31 May if first used for the enterprise income tax final settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late audit makes the annual filings incomplete and exposes the entity to Accounting Law/Company Law penalties and false-report sanctions under the Foreign Investment Law; unresolved non-compliance may result in regulator-declared loss of good standing and compulsory deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture the independent audit is mandatory by legal form: there is no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption. Any foreign-invested enterprise, including a dormant entity, must appoint a PRC-licensed accounting firm to audit its annual financial statements each year. The quantitative threshold is effectively zero for FIEs; audit requirement is triggered by registration as a foreign-invested limited liability company under the Foreign Investment Law and PRC Company Law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS / China GAAP) issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially IFRS-converged; statutory financial statements and audit reports must be prepared in Chinese. Smaller enterprises may use the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards only where legally permitted, but this does not exempt the FIE from the mandatory annual certified audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual SAMR Enterprise Information Publicity Report serves as the annual actual controller and equity confirmation; the JV must identify every individual who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of equity/voting rights or otherwise exercises actual control. Any shareholding or beneficial-ownership change must be reported to SAMR within 30 days of the change. The annual confirmation deadline is the 30 June annual report deadline; knowingly false UBO data triggers administrative penalties and inclusion on the abnormal-operations credit list.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 4,500 (annual registered address / local corporate agent fee, dependent on city and provider)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 10,000 (typical PRC CPA firm quote for a virtual CFO/bookkeeping services entity with multicurrency ledgers)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory concessions include a 15% preferential Enterprise Income Tax rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises, a 15% rate for key encouraged software and integrated circuit enterprises, a 20% low-profit rate effectively reduced to 5% for taxable income up to RMB 3 million in the 2023-2027 concession window, a 100%-200% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures, and sector-specific waivers for encouraged agriculture and infrastructure projects. For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture providing outsourced virtual CFO services, the principal commercially available relief is the general 25% headline rate plus factual cost deductions; free-zone patent box relief is not automatic and depends on separate licensing and substantive office activity within a designated zone.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Form A, 2017 Revision) and its 37-odd supporting schedules; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau e-Tax portal. Quarterly provisional filings also use the EIT prepayment return on the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement plus quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns must be filed and settled within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual corporate income tax reconciliation return for a calendar-year enterprise is due by May 31 of the following year. Social insurance and bookkeeping deadlines are separate and do not extend the EIT deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name, unified social credit code, registered address, legal representative, date of incorporation, industry code ISIC 6920, enterprise type as Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, and tax registration category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the JV's Chinese tax identification data. The non-resident shareholder does not file this return; the JV is a withholding agent for outbound profit distributions, and its non-resident shareholding structure must separately be visible in the equity relations schedule for treaty rate reviews.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of the accounting year, fiscal-year end, currency used in the accounting ledgers, and whether the entity uses a standard 12-month accounting period or an approved non-calendar fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the filing to a Dec 31 year-end unless a special period is approved. If the non-resident receives fees for cross-border digital CFO advice, review whether services are physically performed in China or create a permanent establishment through a dependent agent; such fees could become China-source taxable income requiring separate withholding or PE-apportioned return filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before income tax expense as reported in the audited financial statements, prepared under the PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tie the entry to the Chinese audit report. Profit and loss from outsourced virtual CFO services must be supported by service contracts, time sheets, deliverables, fee invoices, and bank receipts. Cross-border income attributable to non-resident offshore work should be documented if treaty sourcing or PE defenses are later invoked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income through detailed adjustment items: non-deductible entertainment expenses, unapproved provisions, intercompany charges exceeding arm's length, tax-exempt qualified domestic dividends, R&D super deduction, and other permitted deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Closely exam outbound payments to affiliated management companies, virtual CFO offices, or IP holding entities. If the non-resident provider renders no substantive service from its own personnel and the local JV management actually performs the CFO functions, the payment must be disallowed or recharacterized as a transfer-pricing adjustment; avoid deducting WHT on abusive royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of prior-year losses carried forward and offset against current-year taxable income within the statutory five-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a Chinese permanent establishment, losses memorialized in this schedule may be carried forward for five years but only against profit attributable to that same PE. Passive dividend, interest or royalty income subject to final withholding cannot be offset by operating losses of the JV or the non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 25% statutory rate, preferential rates, tax credits, foreign tax credit, withholding credits, and net income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not combine non-resident passive China-source income with the JV's operating income here. The JV remains liable to withhold 10% (or a treaty-reduced rate) on any dividend, interest, or royalty paid to a non-resident; credits and incentives are computed at the entity level, not at the non-resident shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident enterprises, including the amount of foreign enterprise income tax withheld at source and any treaty rate used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before declaring a dividend to the non-resident shareholder, file the Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return and the Non-resident Enterprise Enjoyment of Tax Treaty Treatment Information Report. Provide the shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate, a Beneficial Owner Declaration proving the recipient is not a conduit, shareholding tenure evidence, and a board distribution resolution; retain all records for ten years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 generally, increased to RMB 2,000-10,000 where the violation is serious. Unpaid or underpaid tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% from the statutory due date. Intentional understatement of taxable income with false invoices or omitted revenue violates Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law, exposing the JV to recovery of evaded tax plus a fine of 50%-500% of the tax underpaid; if the amount is large, the responsible person may face imprisonment for up to 3 years under Criminal Law Article 201, extended to 3-7 years with fines if the amount is enormous.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% effective WHT rate on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise with no Chinese establishment or place of business; the statutory nominal rate of 20% is reduced to 10% under EIT Law Articles 3, 4 and 37 and Implementation Regulations Article 91. Bilateral DTAs may reduce this to 10%, or to 5% where the treaty contains a qualified-company article and the recipient holds at least 25% of the equity during the applicable holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence competent authority, submit the completed Report on Non-resident Enterprises Enjoying Tax Treaty Treatment and Beneficial Owner Declaration through the e-Tax portal, and evidence that it has economic substance, actual decision-making, personnel, and funds and is not a conduit. On audit, the tax authority may apply the Principal Purpose Test and reject treaty benefits for arrangements whose main purpose is treaty shopping. The Chinese payer may withhold at the reduced rate once the claim is filed, but must retain the full supporting chain: TRC, share register, dividend resolution, payment instructions, audited financials, and intercompany board minutes for at least ten years, and is required to refile amended withholding if the claim is denied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound interest and royalties to a non-resident without a Chinese PE is 10% each. Treaty rates commonly range from 5% to 10% for interest and from 5% to 10% for royalties, depending on the applicable DTA and the beneficial owner. Outbound royalty and management fees are subject to source tax even if paid under a foreign service agreement; loans from non-bank related parties are restricted by thin-capitalization rules generally allowing a debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1, with excess interest recharacterized as a dividend subject to WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is mandatory for a tax year in which annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property or financial asset transfers, and RMB 40 million for provision of services. A Master File is required when the worldwide group's consolidated revenue in the preceding fiscal year exceeded RMB 5.5 billion and the group engaged in related-party transactions; below those thresholds the JV must still file the annual Statement on Related Party Transactions with its EIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but its General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Article 47, Implementation Rules Article 120) allows full recharacterization of arrangements lacking reasonable commercial substance. For an outsourced virtual CFO service JV, the Chinese entity must be the actual entrepreneur exercising functions, owning relevant assets, controlling risks, and employing decision-making staff. A circular structure using an offshore invoicing shell to divert management fees, royalties, or dividend profits will be challenged under substance-over-form, Controlled Foreign Company rules under EIT Law Article 45, beneficial ownership denial, and permanent establishment attribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through understated service revenue and false invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV receives USD client fees through Stripe and Wise services but deliberately omits a portion of those receivables from the accounting books, issues VAT invoices for non-existent administrative costs from a shell supplier, and files a zero-profit EIT return despite bank deposits materially exceeding reported revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law permits the tax authority to recover the unpaid tax, impose late-payment interest of 0.05% per day, and levy a fine of 50%-500% of the tax evaded. Where the evaded tax amount reaches the criminal threshold, Criminal Law Article 201 imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years on the directly responsible officers and accountants, and 3-7 years plus fines for extremely large evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law when the shareholder or director misuses JV legal personality and asset segregation to evade taxes and divert corporate funds to personal accounts, exposing the director to joint and several restitution. The legal representative and actual controller become subject to the tax authority's joint-punishment blacklist: assets of the individual and spouse may be frozen, the director is placed on a social-credit blacklist, departure from Mainland China is blocked, and the individual may lose eligibility to serve as a director of any PRC company for serious tax violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing fraud and hollow cross-border CFO service fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The directors sign an intercompany management service agreement with a Hong Kong or Singapore affiliate that owns no personnel, no office, no data systems, and no risk-bearing functions; the affiliate charges the JV a 20% annual service fee on total revenue solely to erode Chinese taxable profit, and the JV claims the fee as deductible while failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 41 requires arm's length pricing and Article 48 authorizes a primary transfer-pricing adjustment plus interest computed at the base RMB central bank lending rate plus 5 percentage points. Article 47 GAAR permits the tax authority to disregard or recharacterize the scheme. Failure to file contemporaneous documentation under SAT Announcement 2016 No.42 attracts a documentation penalty of RMB 2,000-10,000, but the higher exposure is the compensatory adjustment and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who executed the intercompany agreements and orchestrated the circular fee payments are jointly and severally liable if the court finds abuse of corporate personality to strip Chinese assets; personal bank accounts of the controlling director may be attached for the assessed corporate tax. If the sham affiliate was knowingly used to falsify costs, the director becomes an accomplice in tax evasion, with criminal imprisonment up to 7 years, fines, a SAFE foreign-exchange penalty, and a personal travel ban recorded in the joint punishment system.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive treaty benefit and intentional failure to withhold on disguised dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident shareholder converts a dividend distribution into a fictitious shareholder loan repayment and a high-rate trademark royalty paid to a zero-tax intermediary holding company with no personnel, no substantive transaction, and no right to use the IP, thereby reducing Chinese WHT from 10% or treaty-reduced 5% to near zero. The JV deliberately does not file the withholding return and does not deduct WHT from the remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under SAT Announcement 2018 No.9 on Beneficial Owner and the Principal Purpose Test applicable under China's DTAs and certain MLI positions, the loan and royalty are recharacterized as dividends; the tax authority collects the differential WHT, imposes late-payment interest, and may apply a fine of 50%-300% of the amount that should have been withheld under Article 69 of the Tax Administration Law. Intentional concealment of the withholding obligation triggers the same tax-evasion penalties as Article 63, including fines of 50%-500% of underpaid tax and criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and finance director are personally accountable for the failure to withhold: the tax authority may enforce the fine and, if the director personally received funds disguised as loan repayments, observe the corporate veil for personal asset seizure and restitution. The non-resident director may be placed on the July 2018-style serious tax violator blacklist, barred from high-consumption activities, refused exit from China, disqualified from acting as a director or supervisor of any company in China, and criminally prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 201 for evading hundreds of thousands of RMB in withholding tax, with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines.
